s2-bubble-sort.trick: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs, bubbling the largest unsorted element to the end each pass. Stop early if a pass makes no swaps — the array is already sorted.

s2-insertion-sort.trick: Build the sorted prefix one element at a time: take the next element and shift larger elements right until it finds its spot — like sorting playing cards in your hand.

s2-merge-sort.trick: Split the array in half recursively until pieces are size 1, then merge sorted halves back together by repeatedly taking the smaller of the two fronts.

s2-quick-sort.trick: Pick a pivot (the first element here), partition the array so smaller elements end up left of it and larger ones right, then recursively sort each side.
s2-quick-sort.time: O(n log n) average, O(n²) worst case

s2-recursive-bubble-sort.trick: Same idea as bubble sort — one pass bubbles the largest remaining element to the end — but each pass is a recursive call on a shrinking prefix instead of an outer loop.

s2-recursive-insertion-sort.trick: Recursively sort the first n-1 elements first, then insert the nth element into its correct position by shifting larger elements right.

s2-selection-sort.trick: Find the minimum in the unsorted part of the array and swap it to the front. Repeat for each position.
